# Style catalog

## apple-keynote-minimal - Apple Keynote Minimal

Pure black or white stage, huge clean type, one product hero and calm, measured springs.

- **Best for**: Premium product or hardware reveals, major version launches; Brand films where restraint signals quality
- **Avoid when**: The audience needs to see the product being used (use ui-camera-tour); The feed rewards high energy and fast hooks (use saas-launch-promo or kinetic-typography)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion). HeyGen ships four re-brandable Apple-style launch compositions in hyperframes-launches, and CSS masks plus GSAP eases express the look directly. Remotion has a measured Apple-recap skill (apple-motion) if you prefer React.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 20-40 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: logo, screenshots
- **Audio**: music
- **Variants**: `light-stage` - #F5F5F7 background, #1D1D1F type; product shadow is the only depth cue.; `fast-recap` - Event-recap pacing - 0.5-1 s shots cut on the beat, full-frame type alternating black and white.
- **Evidence**: 3 public examples (medium)
- **Recipe**: `styles/apple-keynote-minimal.md`

## card-explainer - Card Explainer

An article or deck turned into a narrated sequence of clean animated cards - one key sentence per card.

- **Best for**: Turning blog posts, WeChat or Feishu articles, READMEs, PDFs or slide decks into 1-3 minute videos; Course, training and Bilibili-style knowledge videos
- **Avoid when**: The idea needs relationships between parts drawn out (use dark-diagram-explainer); It is a short, punchy hype piece (use kinetic-typography); There is presenter footage to work with (use talking-head-overlay)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion). Most Chinese-language examples are Codex or Claude Code plus HyperFrames; cards are plain HTML and CSS, and HyperFrames ships an official /slideshow skill. Remotion works equally well.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 45-180 s; difficulty 1/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, music
- **Variants**: `marp-slides` - Markdown (Marp) slides as the source; each slide becomes a scene and its elements reveal in narration order.; `vertical-feed` - 1080x1920 feed version, card at 85% width, larger key sentence, captions above the bottom safe zone.
- **Evidence**: 6 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/card-explainer.md`

## character-dialogue - Character Dialogue Explainer

Two mascots talk over a blackboard, mouths flapping to TTS, with a caption box under every line.

- **Best for**: Long-form explainers and news digests that need a friendly voice (the Japanese Zundamon / VOICEVOX format); Corporate training and course videos made at volume
- **Avoid when**: The brand needs a premium or serious tone (use dark-diagram-explainer or apple-keynote-minimal); The video is under 20 s (use karaoke-caption-short)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). The most-copied open template (remotion-voicevox-template, MIT) is Remotion; per-line Sequences driven by audio durations and sprite swaps per frame are simple React state. HyperFrames works the same way with GSAP timelines.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 30 s - 10 min; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, music, sfx
- **Variants**: `single-host` - One character beside the board in lecture mode.; `slide-board` - The board shows slide images per section instead of chalk drawings.; `vertical` - 1080x1920 with the board on top and both characters side by side below.
- **Evidence**: 6 public examples (medium)
- **Recipe**: `styles/character-dialogue.md`

## cinematic-hud-reel - Cinematic HUD Reel

Fast premium sizzle - motion blur, glow, camera hits, HUD overlays and a logo finale, all synced to code-made sound.

- **Best for**: Personal-brand or creator intros, channel trailers; Showpiece reels that demonstrate what an agent can do; Hype openers for events, AI model or tool teasers
- **Avoid when**: Viewers must read or understand details (use dark-diagram-explainer or ui-camera-tour); The brand is calm or premium-minimal (use apple-keynote-minimal)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion). Layered CSS glow, filters, blend modes and GSAP timelines make HUD choreography cheap to write; several public reels pair HyperFrames with Python-generated sound. Remotion works equally well with @remotion/motion-blur.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 15-40 s; difficulty 3/3
- **Needs from user**: logo
- **Audio**: music, sfx
- **Variants**: `clean-tech` - Fewer HUD layers, glass panels and soft glow; slower 1 s shots for product teasers.; `vertical-intro` - 9:16, 10-15 s personal intro - name, role, three keywords, handle.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (medium)
- **Recipe**: `styles/cinematic-hud-reel.md`

## code-terminal-walkthrough - Code & Terminal Walkthrough

Syntax-highlighted code types itself, diffs morph line by line and a terminal runs the result.

- **Best for**: Developer-tool launches, library and API tutorials, changelog or PR videos; Dev-rel posts on X, YouTube and LinkedIn
- **Avoid when**: The audience is non-technical (use saas-launch-promo or card-explainer); The concept matters more than the code (use dark-diagram-explainer); The subject is a graphical product UI (use ui-camera-tour)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion, motion-canvas). Code blocks are native HTML with Shiki highlighting, and HyperFrames ships a code-diff block and a code-editorial frame preset. Remotion's Code Hike template is the best choice for token-level morphs; Motion Canvas has a strong Code node but weak headless rendering.
- **Format**: 16:9, 1:1; 20-90 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: music, sfx, voiceover, captions
- **Variants**: `retro-crt-terminal` - Green or amber phosphor on black, scanlines, glitch flashes, pixel font and ASCII progress bars - a hacker-style self-intro.; `pr-to-video` - A pull request as a short video - PR title card, 2-3 diffs, before/after result.
- **Evidence**: 4 public examples (medium)
- **Recipe**: `styles/code-terminal-walkthrough.md`

## dark-diagram-explainer - Dark Diagram Explainer

Narrated, faceless explainer - SVG diagrams build piece by piece on a dark canvas, synced to the voice.

- **Best for**: Explaining a technical concept, tool, architecture or piece of news; Faceless channels on YouTube, Shorts, Bilibili and Douyin
- **Avoid when**: The content is a list of quotes from an article (use card-explainer); The subject is equations or proofs (use math-manim); The subject is real code (use code-terminal-walkthrough); It is a marketing piece with no explanation (use saas-launch-promo)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). Most public examples use Remotion; the narration timeline maps directly onto Sequences and calculateMetadata. HyperFrames ships an official /faceless-explainer workflow skill.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 30-120 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, music, sfx
- **Variants**: `black-canvas-neon` - Pure black with a star-field or dot-field backdrop, white line art plus one purple accent, a HUD capsule on top and a chapter progress bar at the bottom; long-form 3-5 min.; `vertical-short` - 1080x1920, 30-45 s, diagram in the middle third, larger captions, hook within 1.5 s.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/dark-diagram-explainer.md`

## data-story-charts - Data Story Charts

Charts, counters and rankings that build over time, one insight per scene.

- **Best for**: Metrics announcements, reports and survey results; Top-N rankings, bar-chart races and year-in-review recaps
- **Avoid when**: There is no real dataset (use kinetic-typography or saas-launch-promo); The story is mainly geographic routes or regions (a dedicated map style is still in the v2 backlog); The topic needs a step-by-step concept explanation (use dark-diagram-explainer)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). Data lives in props or JSON and every chart is a pure function of the frame; calculateMetadata can size the video from the row count. HyperFrames has a ready bar-chart-race block.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1; 20-60 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: data
- **Audio**: music, sfx, voiceover
- **Variants**: `ranking-countdown` - Top-N countdown or bar-chart race - rank cards or sorted bars re-ordering per period, the winner gets a burst.; `year-in-review` - Personal or company recap - activity over time, top categories, best month callouts, warm accent.
- **Evidence**: 6 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/data-story-charts.md`

## flat-cartoon-explainer - Flat Cartoon Explainer

Bright flat-vector pop-science with a simple host character and code-drawn figures, every action pinned to a narration word.

- **Best for**: Pop-science, kids' education and "how does X work" explainers on YouTube and Bilibili; Friendly product or service explainers for non-technical audiences
- **Avoid when**: The audience is technical and expects precision (use dark-diagram-explainer or math-manim); The story needs realistic character acting, walking or turning (code-drawn rigs look broken)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion). The documented pop-science pipelines draw characters on Canvas and SVG inside HyperFrames with GSAP timelines keyed to narration words. Remotion with inline SVG components is an equal alternative.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 45 s - 6 min; difficulty 3/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, music, sfx
- **Variants**: `flat-cutout` - Paper-cutout look with an offset drop shadow and slight rotation jitter between poses.; `vertical-short` - 1080x1920 with the host on top, the concept in the middle and captions below.; `icon-infographic` - No characters; flat icons and labels in the same palette carry the story.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/flat-cartoon-explainer.md`

## karaoke-caption-short - Karaoke Caption Short

Vertical faceless short where huge word-by-word highlighted captions are the visual, carried by a TTS voice.

- **Best for**: Faceless TikTok, Douyin, Reels and Shorts channels at volume; Turning a script, article or thread into a narrated short in minutes
- **Avoid when**: The topic needs diagrams to be understood (use dark-diagram-explainer or card-explainer); You have talking-head footage (use talking-head-overlay)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). @remotion/captions groups word timings into TikTok-style pages and the official TikTok captions template is built on it. HyperFrames ships about 20 ready caption components (pill-karaoke, kinetic-slam and more).
- **Format**: 9:16; 20-60 s; difficulty 1/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, music
- **Variants**: `single-word` - One word at a time, 140-180 px, dead center; maximum energy.; `pill-karaoke` - The whole sentence stays on screen and a colored pill slides under the active word.; `template-swap-series` - Scene components stay fixed and only the script changes per episode, for daily series.
- **Evidence**: 7 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/karaoke-caption-short.md`

## kinetic-typography - Kinetic Typography

An empty stage and one word at a time - type appears, settles and exits exactly on the beat.

- **Best for**: Manifestos, announcements, quotes and teasers with no visuals available; Music-led social shorts and lyric videos; Openers and section breaks inside longer videos
- **Avoid when**: The message needs a product shown (use ui-camera-tour or saas-launch-promo); There is narration to follow word for word (use karaoke-caption-short)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion). Type set in HTML/CSS with GSAP timelines is the shortest path from a beat list to motion, and public examples (GPTers 30 s piece, bang-motion) are HTML-based. Remotion works the same way with spring and interpolate.
- **Format**: 9:16, 16:9, 1:1; 15-45 s; difficulty 1/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: music
- **Variants**: `poster-color-block` - Huge cropped words and solid color fields slamming in on the beat, 3-4 color palette.; `lyric-mv` - Lyrics from a timed SRT, each line in its own layout, words landing on vocal onsets.; `webgl-type` - Condensed display type over procedural three.js terrain or liquid backgrounds with HUD micro-type.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/kinetic-typography.md`

## math-manim - Math Explainer (Manim)

3Blue1Brown-style - geometry and equations morph step by step on a dark canvas, paced for understanding.

- **Best for**: Math, physics, algorithms and machine-learning concepts; Teaching videos on YouTube and Bilibili
- **Avoid when**: There are no formulas or geometry (use dark-diagram-explainer); The subject is code itself (use code-terminal-walkthrough); It is marketing (use saas-launch-promo)
- **Tool**: manim (alt: motion-canvas). Manim Community is purpose-built for this look - LaTeX typesetting, coordinate systems and term-matching transforms - and is actively maintained. Motion Canvas suits the same look but has slowed down and lacks a first-class headless render.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 60-300 s; difficulty 3/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, music
- **Variants**: `algorithm-viz` - Arrays as squares, pointers as arrows, swaps and comparisons animated; sorting, search and graph traversal.; `vertical-short` - 1080x1920 one-concept short, 30-60 s, equation in the top third and geometry below.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (medium)
- **Recipe**: `styles/math-manim.md`

## painterly-canvas - Painterly Canvas

Watercolor washes and ink brush strokes painted procedurally on canvas, seeded so every frame renders the same way twice.

- **Best for**: Lyric videos, poems, story moments and emotional brand pieces; Creators who want a hand-made look without image or video models
- **Avoid when**: Precise information must be read (use card-explainer or data-story-charts); Render time is tight; watercolor fills are slow (use flat-cartoon-explainer)
- **Tool**: html-capture (alt: hyperframes). p5.js + p5.brush gives real watercolor and ink brushes, but p5 is not natively seekable; the raw capture contract (window.renderFrame(i, fps) redraws frame i from scratch, captured by scripts/capture_html.mjs) keeps it deterministic. A seekable canvas inside HyperFrames is the alternative.
- **Format**: 1:1, 9:16, 16:9; 15-60 s; difficulty 3/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: music, captions
- **Variants**: `ink-sumi` - Black ink on rice paper with a single vermilion seal accent and brush calligraphy titles.; `painted-reveal` - Line art reveals left to right, then washes fill in the same direction.; `abstract-flow` - No characters; flowing brush fields that react to the music's amplitude.
- **Evidence**: 4 public examples (medium)
- **Recipe**: `styles/painterly-canvas.md`

## pixel-retro - Pixel Retro

An 8-bit world from palette grids, with chunky sprites, pixel fonts, stepped motion and beat-synced cuts.

- **Best for**: Vertical music videos, PSAs and playful brand shorts for Douyin, TikTok and Reels; Game, indie-dev and nostalgia-themed promos
- **Avoid when**: The audience expects a premium or corporate tone (use apple-keynote-minimal or saas-launch-promo); Real product UI must be shown legibly (use ui-camera-tour)
- **Tool**: hyperframes (alt: remotion). Most public pixel shorts were made with HyperFrames; a canvas drawn at logical size and scaled with image-rendering pixelated is plain HTML, and GSAP steps() eases give stepped motion. Remotion works equally with a canvas per frame.
- **Format**: 9:16, 16:9; 15-60 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: script
- **Audio**: music, sfx, captions
- **Variants**: `crt-terminal` - Green or amber phosphor terminal with typing, glitches and ASCII progress bars.; `pixel-brand-short` - 15 s vertical brand piece with the logo rebuilt as a pixel sprite.; `side-scroller` - 16:9 side-scrolling level where each stage is a point of the explanation.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/pixel-retro.md`

## procedural-3d-sting - Procedural 3D Sting

A short, mostly wordless 3D or shader reveal - particles, glass and light converge into a logo.

- **Best for**: Logo stings, channel or app openers, game and festival intros; 5-15 s teasers where mood matters more than information
- **Avoid when**: The video must explain features (use saas-launch-promo or ui-camera-tour); The machine renders WebGL slowly or not at all headless (use kinetic-typography)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). @remotion/three wraps React Three Fiber so every transform is a function of useCurrentFrame, which keeps 3D deterministic; several public stings use exactly this stack. HyperFrames also renders seekable Three.js scenes.
- **Format**: 16:9, 1:1; 6-15 s; difficulty 3/3
- **Needs from user**: logo
- **Audio**: music, sfx
- **Variants**: `shader-only` - A single full-screen GLSL fragment shader driven by time = frame / fps; no meshes.; `particle-logo` - Points sampled from the logo SVG fly in from a noise field and lock into the mark.; `power-on` - Fictional console or device power-on - scanline flash, chrome logo, synth chime.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/procedural-3d-sting.md`

## saas-launch-promo - SaaS Launch Promo

Dark canvas, one brand accent, kinetic headlines and floating UI cards cut to the beat.

- **Best for**: App, SaaS or browser-extension launch on X, Product Hunt or LinkedIn; Feature announcement teasers (15-45 s)
- **Avoid when**: The message needs explanation or narration (use dark-diagram-explainer); The brand is warm, playful or consumer-lifestyle (use flat-cartoon-explainer or glass variant)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). Most public examples use Remotion; springs, Series and TransitionSeries map directly onto beat-cut scene lists. HyperFrames + GSAP is equally capable and Apache-2.0.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 20-45 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: logo, screenshots
- **Audio**: music, sfx
- **Variants**: `glass-gradient` - Soft animated mesh gradient, frosted-glass cards, emoji or icon glyphs; friendlier consumer tone.; `vertical-teaser` - 9:16, 15 s cut-down with stacked layout for Reels, Shorts and Douyin.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/saas-launch-promo.md`

## talking-head-overlay - Talking-Head Overlay Package

Lower thirds, glass badges, step numbers and data callouts pinned to the speaker's words, never covering the face.

- **Best for**: Knowledge creators and founders who already record talking-head videos; Turning a plain interview, vlog or course recording into a produced piece
- **Avoid when**: There is no footage at all (use karaoke-caption-short or dark-diagram-explainer); The video is mainly a product demo (use ui-camera-tour)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes). Remotion's OffthreadVideo, word-timed captions and ProRes 4444 / WebM alpha export cover both the composited and the overlay-only deliverable. HyperFrames ships an official talking-head-recut skill and also exports transparent layers.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; footage length (30 s - 20 min); difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: footage, script
- **Audio**: voiceover, captions, sfx
- **Variants**: `overlay-only` - No footage in the render; a transparent ProRes 4444 or WebM-alpha layer the editor drops above the footage.; `pip-split` - The speaker shrinks to a rounded picture-in-picture while a panel, chart or quote fills the rest of the frame.; `vertical-talk` - 1080x1920 talking head with captions in the lower band and badges in the upper band.
- **Evidence**: 8 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/talking-head-overlay.md`

## ui-camera-tour - UI Camera Tour

The real product UI as the set - the camera pushes in on whatever gets clicked, with 2.5D tilt, cursor and beat cuts.

- **Best for**: Product demos, feature walkthroughs, changelog videos; Landing-page hero videos and onboarding clips
- **Avoid when**: There is no product UI yet (use saas-launch-promo or kinetic-typography); The topic is a concept rather than a workflow (use dark-diagram-explainer)
- **Tool**: remotion (alt: hyperframes, html-capture). A camera is just a transform on a world container, and Remotion's interpolate plus @remotion/motion-blur make zoom targets and blur precise; the strongest public recipe library (video-shotcraft) is Remotion. HyperFrames or a raw Playwright capture suit UIs that already exist as HTML.
- **Format**: 16:9, 9:16; 30-60 s; difficulty 2/3
- **Needs from user**: screenshots, logo
- **Audio**: music, sfx, voiceover
- **Variants**: `website-scroll` - Long-page capture scrolled with eased stops at each section, callouts popping beside it.; `mobile-device` - 9:16 phone frame; taps instead of cursor clicks, screen transitions as in the app.
- **Evidence**: 5 public examples (strong)
- **Recipe**: `styles/ui-camera-tour.md`
